title: Blood Microplastics in Neurovascular Patients and Healthy Volunteers: An Exploratory Study of Disease-Specific Differences, Variability, and Determinants
summary: Microplastics are very small plastic particles that can enter the human body through food, drinking water, or inhalation. These particles have been detected in the human body, including in the bloodstream. The health implications of this finding are not yet fully understood; however, initial evidence suggests possible associations with certain cardiovascular diseases. This study investigates how many microplastic particles are present in the blood of healthy individuals and of patients with diseases affecting the blood vessels supplying the brain. For this purpose, a single venous blood sample is collected and analyzed in a specialized laboratory. In some healthy participants, additional blood samples are taken at different time points to better understand natural fluctuations and the influence of various conditions. The results are expected to improve our understanding of microplastic exposure in humans and potential links to specific diseases.
conditions: microplastic exposure and possible associations with neurovascular dieseases

interventions.name:
Patients with neurovascular diseases
Study procedure: Single venous blood draw (approx. 5 ml) for microplastic particle analysis. No additional study-related interventions.

Healthy volunteers
Study procedure: Single or repeated venous blood draws (up to 3 draws, approx. 5 ml each) for microplastic particle analysis. No additional study-related interventions.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Written informed consent
- For patients: Presence of a neurovascular disease (e.g., ischemic stroke or intracranial aneurysm)
- For healthy volunteers: No known cardiovascular, metabolic, or chronic inflammatory diseases
Exclusion criteria:
- Lack of informed consent
- Pregnancy or breastfeeding
- Acute or chronic infections
- Known relevant cardiovascular, metabolic, or inflammatory diseases (for healthy volunteers)
